summary: Fifteen findings confirmed, two rejected. Rejected: /1 and /13 misread Theorem 4.10's hypothesis. In the paper 'the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad' is the stabilizer of ρ̄ (a tuple in Ĝ) under conjugation, i.e. Z_Ĝ(ρ̄) = Z_Ĝ (TeX l. 492, 509, 675), not the centralizer of the image in Ĝ^ad; so the extraction's Schur's-lemma sentence for GL_n and the introduction are right, and the proposed replacement would be false (the Borel subgroup of GL_2). Confirmed with corrected fixes: /2 (item 34 is a source of GS.5 beside LAFFORGUE-18/41, still missing), /3 (single owner IHG.1, allowing disconnected H), /4 (split item 21: the Bernstein presentation to the accepted SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, Casselman to SR.2), /5 (Proposition 8.3 to LP3), /7 (framed deformations from R08.1 per PASKUNAS-QUAST-26; unframed Def and Lemma 5.9 to R04.1/R04.2), /6 (Weil II bound owner DWP.7; Chin's Theorem 4.6 already at GS.6; Proposition 11.2 needs flat Cassels–Poitou–Tate, unplanned), /10 (affects the proof of Theorem 11.8 rather than a stated result), /15 (drop element (g); (a) and (d) are errors), /16 (item 27 copies the paper), /17 (the false 'not open access' claim also sits in all 16 searched fields). Confirmed as stated: /8, /9, /11 (the G₂ counterexample checks), /12, /14. Every confirmed paper mistake is also in the published Acta text. Nine of the twelve published-page locators the review added are off by one or two pages; the fixer for /17 should correct them.

sources.citation: arXiv:1609.03491v2 and its LaTeX source (the version the extraction read).

findings.reason: The extraction does say, in item 11, the summary, route 3's reason, route 1's brief and the report, that for GL_n the hypothesis of Theorem 4.10 is Schur's lemma and that the statement is Carayol's. The finding's Q_8 counterexample depends on reading 'the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad_k' as the centralizer in Ĝ^ad of the projected image ad∘ρ̄(Γ). That is not the paper's notion. Throughout, the paper means the stabilizer of ρ̄ under the conjugation action of Ĝ^ad on Ĝ: the elements s of Ĝ^ad with Ad(s)ρ̄(γ) = ρ̄(γ) exactly in Ĝ. The text shows this in five places. (1) The proof of Theorem 4.10 (arXiv v2 p. 17; Acta p. 26, not p. 25) applies Proposition 3.13 to a point x = (ḡ_1, …, ḡ_n) of X_n = Ĝ^n with 'scheme-theoretically trivial centralizer in Ĝ^ad_k', where Ĝ^ad acts on Ĝ^n by conjugation. For a point, this can only mean the stabilizer, and Proposition 3.13 needs exactly that. (2) The remark after Proposition 3.13 says the same. (3) The proof of Lemma 5.1 and the deformation-functor construction use the triviality to get a free action of Ĝ^{ad,∧} on lifts. (4) The proof of Proposition 6.6 writes g ρ_λ^σ g^{-1} = ρ_λ with g in Ĝ^ad and calls Z_{Ĝ^ad}(ρ_λ(Frob)) a centralizer. (5) Decisively, the proof of Proposition 10.7(i) says it is 'enough to show that Z_{Ĝ^ad_k}(φ(Γ)) is scheme-theoretically trivial, or even that Z_{Ĝ_k}(φ(Γ)) = Z_{Ĝ_k}'. That implication holds for the stabilizer (lift s fppf-locally to Ĝ; the lift centralizes φ, so it is central). It fails for the finding's notion. Take Ĝ = SL_2 and a dihedral Coxeter parameter: the image of diag(i, −i) in PGL_2 commutes with the dihedral image, since it conjugates the Weyl element to its negative. So under the finding's reading, Proposition 10.7(i) would be false for SL_2 and in every type with non-trivial centre, and the paper's remark that simple connectedness is what makes (i) true would make no sense. With the paper's notion, the hypothesis is Z_Ĝ(ρ̄) = Z_Ĝ scheme-theoretically. For GL_n this says End_Γ(k^n) = k. Together with absolute complete reducibility, which Theorem 4.10 also assumes, this is equivalent to absolute irreducibility by Schur's lemma, exactly as the extraction says. For Q_8 ⊂ SL_2(F̄_l), l odd: Ad([i]) sends j to −j ≠ j, so [i] does not fix ρ̄. The stabilizer is Z_{GL_2}(Q_8)/G_m = 1. So Q_8 satisfies Theorem 4.10's hypothesis, and V_4 is the centralizer of a different object. Nothing needs fixing. Optionally, item 11 could say 'the centralizer of ρ̄ for the conjugation action of Ĝ^ad, equivalently Z_Ĝ(ρ̄) = Z_Ĝ scheme-theoretically' to prevent this misreading. Note also that the finding's proposed replacement sentence would itself be wrong: trivial centralizer in PGL_n does not imply absolute irreducibility without complete reducibility. For example, the Borel subgroup of GL_2 (l ≠ 2) has trivial scheme-theoretic stabilizer in PGL_2 but is reducible. Lead verifier's check: the paper's own usage fixes the meaning. TeX l. 492 and l. 509 (Proposition 3.10 and the paragraph after it) take X = Ĝ^n with G = Ĝ^ad acting by simultaneous conjugation and ask that the stabilizer Z_{G_k}(x) of the point x = (g_1, …, g_n) ∈ Ĝ^n(k) be scheme-theoretically trivial; l. 675 speaks of 'the scheme-theoretic centralizer of ρ̄(Γ) in Ĝ^ad_k', again the elements of Ĝ^ad fixing elements of Ĝ under conjugation. So the hypothesis is Z_{Ĝ}(ρ̄) = Z_{Ĝ} scheme-theoretically, not triviality of the centralizer of the image of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad, and the rejection stands.

Checked against v2 p. 39 and the published text (Proposition 8.10 and its proof on p. 58; the sentence 'It follows from Proposition 8.10 that it is a finite flat O-algebra' and Corollary 8.11 with its proof on p. 59, so the finding's single published locator p. 58 should read pp. 58-59). The paper's proof of Proposition 8.10 is literally 'This will follow from [Lafa, Proposition 13.1]' plus a rewriting of f in Z[Ĝ^n]^{Ĝ×Ĝ} as a matrix coefficient ξ((g_i)·x) by the recipe of Lafforgue's Lemme 10.5. Finite flatness of B(U, O) is immediate: C_cusp(U, O) is a finite torsion-free, hence free, module over the discrete valuation ring O, so any O-subalgebra of its endomorphism ring is finite and torsion-free, hence flat. The passage from level U(N) to an arbitrary U ⊂ ∏ G(O_Kv) is by restriction to U-invariants, which preserves the lattice. The proof of Corollary 8.11 is 'applying Theorem 4.5 to the projection of Θ_U to the quotient B(U, O)/m', i.e. reconstruction over F̄_l; this is Lafforgue's Theorem 13.2 at one maximal ideal (generalized-eigenspace Satake compatibility is exactly 'T_{V,v} = χ_V(σ̄_m(Frob_v)) mod m'). PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18/41 states Proposition 13.1 (the O_E-lattice is preserved by every excursion operator) and Theorem 13.2, and sits in that paper's route 2, a source route to GS.3-GS.5 which PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18.review.json accepts. So once both accepted routes are applied, the same statement is planned in GS.5 and constructed again in the proposed Part II: a genuine duplicate. Both sentences of the item's note are wrong as the finding says: Lafforgue's §13 does give the integral statement (the lattice is preserved, and finite flatness is a one-line consequence), and §3.2 (Proposition 3.13, the slice theorem over a DVR) enters only through Theorem 4.10 ('We will use the following consequence of Proposition 3.13', v2 p. 17, published p. 26), which is used in Lemma 8.19 (v2 p. 45, published p. 68), not in Corollary 8.11. Fix, with one change: do not mark item 34 'planned'. GS.5's stage text in the atlas does not mention integral or mod-l coefficients, and LAFFORGUE-18/41 is itself a 'missing' item that reaches GS.5 only through an accepted source route. Keep item 34 'missing' and route it in a new source route of this extraction to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.5, beside LAFFORGUE-18/41. This is the precedent PAPER-PASKUNAS-QUAST-26 set when it routed its G-pseudocharacter items to the stage this extraction had chosen. The route reason should ask GS.5's node for Proposition 13.1 and Theorem 13.2 to be stated at arbitrary level U ⊂ ∏ G(O_Kv), since the Part II needs Iwahori and pro-prime-to-l levels at Taylor-Wiles places. It should also ask that node to give the finite flat O-algebra B(U, O) with Θ_U valued in it, and the indexing by f ∈ Z[Ĝ^n]^Ĝ via the Lemme 10.5 recipe. Then remove item 34 from route 1's items, change the brief's construction bullet so that it imports B(U, O) and σ̄_m from GS.5 and constructs only the freeness of §8.3 and R = B, and correct both sentences of the note.

Checked the routes and review verdicts. This extraction's route 3 (accepted) sends Definition 4.1, Theorem 4.5, Proposition 4.7 and Theorem 4.10 to IHG.0/IHG.1. PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18's route 3 (accepted) sends /35 (Richardson's closed-orbit theory), /36 (the GL_r pseudo-character case), /37 (Lemme 11.10 and the proof of Proposition 11.7, which is the same reconstruction argument as Theorem 4.5: maximise the dimension of the generated group, minimise the centralizer, define σ(γ) as the unique completion of the tuple) and /42 (the characteristic-l input, which 'refers to the proof of Theorem 4.5 of [BHKT16]') to LP2/LP3, and its reason says 'Plan it once here ... and let both LP2:semisimple-characters and GS.5 import it'. In addition /34 (Proposition 11.7) is planned at GS.5 and LP2:semisimple-characters. The accepted LanglandsParameterStacks decomposition already has the node LP2:semisimple-characters/character-bijection (FS VIII.3.8, over any algebraically closed L over Z_l, which includes characteristic l). The draft GS packet has its own node GS.5/reconstruction-of-a-langlands-parameter with independent proof steps. PAPER-PASKUNAS-QUAST-26 (accepted) routes Quast's reconstruction for disconnected G (its /40) to IHG.1 as well. So one theorem, the bijection between pseudocharacters and completely reducible representations over an algebraically closed field, is being planned at IHG.1, at LP2/LP3 and at GS.5, and the item-8 note's 'cite one proof, not three' is not implemented by any route. Two small inaccuracies do not affect the verdict: the phrase 'reindexing and multiplication relations' is in LP2:integral-invariants, not LP2:excursion-presentation (the evidence quotes the right stage); and GS.5 is a consumer-specialisation rather than a third general home. Fix: choose one owner and record it. I agree with the finding's first option, IHG.1. IHG.0 already plans GL_n pseudocharacters (Chenevier, Taylor) in its packet, and two accepted extractions (this one and PASKUNAS-QUAST-26) put the Ĝ-pseudocharacter definition and its deformation theory there. At stage level IHG.0/IHG.1 have only Mathlib inputs, so the links IHG.1 → LP2:semisimple-characters and IHG.1 → GS.5 create no cycle. The fix needs four additions. (1) The owned statement must be the most general one its users need: a possibly disconnected reductive H with H^0-conjugacy, over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic. LAFFORGUE-18/34 applies it to H = ^LG, FS VIII.3.8 to Ĝ ⋊ Q, and PQ26/40 to disconnected G; BHKT's Theorem 4.5 covers only connected Ĝ. (2) IHG.1 then needs an input link from the stage that owns the closed-orbit and complete-reducibility invariant theory. This extraction's items 4 and 5 and LAFFORGUE-18/35 route that theory to LP2/LP3. (3) Redirect LAFFORGUE-18/37 and /42 to the chosen owner, not only annotate /42, and amend the notes of LAFFORGUE-18/34 and PQ26/40 to name it. (4) Recast the GS.5 packet node and the LP decomposition's character-bijection node as specialisations that import the general theorem and prove only continuity and the Weil-group or global-Galois conventions. If the fixer prefers LP2 instead, the same four points apply with the roles exchanged.

Checked §7 at v2 pp. 28-30 and published pp. 42-44. The Bernstein presentation (7.1) and relation (7.2) are on published p. 43, not p. 42, and Lemma 7.2 is on p. 44. Item 21 contains the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_{U_0} over O with the Bernstein presentation O[X_*(T)] ⊗̃ O[U_0\U/U_0], relation (7.2) and the centrality of O[X_*(T)]^W ([HKP10]). It also contains Casselman's isomorphism π^{U_0} ≅ r_N(π)^{T(O_K)} ([Cas80, Props. 2.4-2.5]), Lemma 7.2 and Lemma 7.1. Read against the atlas stage texts: SR.1 plans convolution Hecke algebras over rings and e_U corners; SR.2 plans induction, Jacquet functors, Frobenius reciprocity and the geometric lemma; SR.4 plans spherical Satake for a hyperspecial K. None of them mentions an Iwahori subgroup, an Iwahori-Hecke algebra, the Bernstein presentation or Casselman's theorem. A search of all stage texts, roadmap READMEs, packets and decompositions finds 'Iwahori-Hecke' and 'Bernstein presentation' nowhere (RG2.4 has only the group-level Iwahori-Bruhat decomposition). Other accepted extractions say the same: BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/16 notes 'the Borel-Casselman comparison ... is planned nowhere', and CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's ext-borel-casselman note says 'The atlas does not plan it'. So 'planned' is wrong. The fix needs correcting, because routing the Bernstein presentation to SR.4 would create a second owner. The accepted PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 route 10 proposes the Part II SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, whose brief says 'Construct the Iwahori Bernstein presentation and the isomorphisms from its center to a parahoric center and spherical Hecke algebra'. PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-ZHU-17 and PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17 have accepted routes that coalesce with it, and CLOZEL-THORNE-17's review moved the Bernstein-Lusztig presentation there precisely because SR.1-SR.3 'do not plan affine Hecke algebra presentations'. Right fix: split item 21. (a) The Iwahori-Hecke algebra over O with its Bernstein presentation, relation (7.2) and the central O[X_*(T)]^W go to a part-ii route that coalesces with SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, as CLOZEL-THORNE-17 route 6 does. It should record that BHKT needs the integral form over O with q ∈ O^× and the normalization e_λ ↦ q^{-⟨ρ,λ⟩}[U_0 λ(ϖ) U_0]. (b) Casselman's isomorphism and Lemma 7.2(i) (the Borel-Casselman theorem, with [BZ77, 2.9]) go as a source of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2, beside the accepted routes of CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (SR.2-SR.4) and BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/16 (SR.1-SR.2). (c) Lemma 7.2(ii), the integrality of χ and the 0-or-1-dimensional localization under trivial Weyl stabilizer of χ̄, is BHKT's own Taylor-Wiles input and joins item 22 in the Part II. (d) Lemma 7.1 is local class field theory composed with the tautological torus duality. It can be marked planned at FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.4 (whose text 'Specialize[s] and prove[s] the local reciprocity construction for F_{q^d}((t))') and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.5 (whose text requires 'the split torus/GL_n examples'). Keep SR.1 as planned for the definitions of H_V and the non-unital inclusions, and correct the report's sentence.

(a) Proposition 8.3 (v2 p. 36, published p. 53): Z[M̂]^{M̂} → Z[T̂]^{W(M̂,T̂)} is an isomorphism for every standard Levi. It is used over the residue field k in §8.3.1 (v2 p. 40: 'the homomorphism H(M(K_v), M(O_Kv)) → k associated to the conjugacy class of ρ_i(Frob_v) (which exists by Proposition 8.3)'), so the integral form is genuinely needed. I checked the statement itself. Injectivity holds because Z[M̂] is torsion-free and the conjugates of T̂ are dense in M̂ over Q. Surjectivity holds because the W-invariants Z[T̂]^W have a Z-basis of dominant orbit sums, and these are unitriangular in the characters of Weyl modules, which are class functions defined over Z. No stage plans this. SR.4 identifies Hecke eigencharacters with semisimple classes over a coefficient field; RG2.5 restricts itself to 'the group and functorial duality data only'; and neither the atlas nor the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap mentions a Chevalley restriction theorem. Item 32 is 'planned' at FA.6/SR.4/RG2.5, its note concedes that Proposition 8.3 is not planned, and route 2 names Proposition 8.3 in its reason but its items are only 4, 5 and 6. So the statement is neither planned nor routed. One wording point: PROTOCOL §16 does allow a source route to name planned items, so 'a planned item cannot be routed' is too strong, but the defect stands. (b) Definition 8.7 and Lemma 8.8 (v2 p. 38, published p. 57) are used twice in the proof of Theorem 11.4 (v2 p. 63, published pp. 94-96), as quoted. GS.5's acceptance line excludes an inverse correspondence, and GS.5 plans only the decomposition by σ. Item 33 is 'planned' at GS.5/GS.7 while its note says 'The one thing not planned anywhere is Definition 8.7 and Lemma 8.8'. Item 29 mentions Lemma 8.8 only as an ingredient, and the brief's GS.5 import does not mention it. Fix as stated, with one precision for (a): route the new Proposition 8.3 item by adding it to route 2's items at LanglandsParameterStacks LP3 rather than RG2.5. LP3 is 'Integral reductive invariant theory' with Weyl and dual-Weyl modules, which is what the proof uses, while RG2.5's text excludes invariant theory. Route 2's reason already says 'belongs with them', and SR.4 and the Part II consume it. For (b), the substantive new content is Lemma 8.8 with its proof through Proposition 6.4 (item 19, Part II); Definition 8.7 is only a name for 'conjugate to some σ_p' built from GS.5's output, so the new item and its route to the Part II are right.

Checked each named input in the paper (v2 pp. 20-21, 26-27, 40-44, 60; the same statements are in the Acta text), in the extraction's items and brief, and in the atlas stage texts and other papers' routes. The brief's 'Import, never re-plan' list names GS.5, GS.7, FA.6, FA.5, RG2.5, R03.1-R03.5, SR.1/2/4, LP2/LP3, IHG.0/IHG.1, R01.1 and R23.1 only. The inputs appear only inside the proof sketches of items 14, 15, 16, 18, 19 and 20 and in the brief's prose (for example 'Weil II purity ([Laf02, Thm. VII.6], [Del80])'), so the design job gets no instruction to import them and could re-plan them, against PROTOCOL section 15; section 16 requires key theorems the paper uses to be items. Point by point. (1) Right: Proposition 5.12 and Theorem 6.5 rest on [Laf02, Theoreme VII.6]; GS.6 plans L. Lafforgue's correspondence 'in both directions' with its 'purity and multiplicity conclusions' (RS-22 keeps this), so it is planned there and should be imported. (2) Right. The exact statement used (H^j of a lisse sheaf, pure of weight 0, on the smooth open curve is mixed of weights >= j) is DWP.7's text: 'For X0 smooth and F lisse of weights >= w, use Poincare duality to prove H^i(X,F) weights >= w+i.' So the owner is DWP.7; DWP.6 only supplies it. (3) Right for Propositions 5.11 and 5.19. Their coefficients are k-vector spaces of characteristic l different from p, and the accepted route 3 of PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22 sends exactly these function-field cases (FKP22/6: finite p-primary modules with p not equal to char F) to R02.3/R02.4. It is not right for Proposition 11.2. There the Cassels-Poitou-Tate sequence of [Ces, Thm 6.2] is applied to the centre Z_G and its Cartier dual. Z_G is of multiplicative type and can have order divisible by p = char K (mu_n with p | n; the paper reduces to mu_n), so this is fppf duality. That is the point of Cesnavicius's 'without restrictions on the order', and no stage plans it, including FKP22's route. (4) Right: no stage mentions de Jong's conjecture (the only 'de Jong' in the atlas is alterations), and FKP22/63 says so. (5) Partly right. Chin's Theorem 4.6 (companions over a number field E for plain sheaves) is already routed to GS.6 by the accepted route 3 of PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 (its item E07). Chin's Theorems 1.4 and 6.12 (independence of l of the monodromy group, which is what Theorem 6.5 needs) and Lemma 6.4 are planned nowhere. PAPER-KLEVDAL-PATRIKIS-25's companion Part II, which would have touched them, was rejected. (6) and (7) Right: Larsen / [SW, Prop. 7.1] and [Vol89] appear in no stage, and the only other Larsen routes (CADORET-HUI-TAMAGAWA-17 route 2) were rejected. (8) The fact is right: Proposition 8.12 takes as data mod-l representations rho_i : Gamma_K -> M^(k) for the cuspidal constituents on every proper Levi M, and Lemma 8.16's proof says only 'We are now in the situation of Proposition 8.12' without constructing them. The routing is wrong, though. The characteristic-zero input is V. Lafforgue's parametrization for the split reductive group M, with finite-order central characters. GS.5 already plans that for general reductive groups and the brief imports it, so GS.5 needs no new source. The step still to supply is the reduction mod l with the Hecke matching mod m_R. It uses Theorem 4.8 / Definition 4.9 (item 10) and Proposition 8.3 for M^ (item 32). Minor: the prerequisites list also names [Mil06], [Ces] and [Vol89], not just (1), (4), (5) and (6). Right fix: add items (1) planned at GS.6; (2) planned at DWP.7; (3a) the Euler characteristic and Poitou-Tate for prime-to-p coefficients, planned at R02.3/R02.4 as their function-field cases per FKP22 route 3; (3b) flat Cassels-Poitou-Tate over a global function field for finite multiplicative-type coefficients of arbitrary order ([Ces, Thm 6.2]), missing, routed to the Part II as an imported black box with [Ces] kept as a prerequisite; (4) de Jong/Gaitsgory, (5') Chin Thms 1.4, 6.12 and Lemma 6.4, (6) [SW, Prop. 7.1]/[Lar95] and (7) [Vol89], each missing and routed to the Part II as a black box or proposed prerequisite extraction; (5'') Chin Thm 4.6, planned at GS.6 via PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25; (8) a missing Part II item, 'residual Galois representations of the cuspidal spectrum of Levis, compatible with Satake mod m_R'. Item (8) depends on GS.5 applied to each Levi M, on item 10 and on item 32, with a note that the paper leaves it implicit. Add GS.6, DWP.7 and R02.3/R02.4 to the brief's import list.

§5.1 (v2 pp. 18-19) is stated for an arbitrary profinite Γ with Mazur's Φ_l, Ĝ semisimple and l very good. Lemma 5.1, Definitions 5.2-5.4, Remark 5.3, Proposition 5.5 (pro-representability via the free Ĝ^{ad,∧}_O-action on liftings) and Proposition 5.6 (presentation by h^1 generators and h^2 relations) use nothing about function fields or shtukas; Lemma 5.9 is likewise abstract. The atlas and accepted routes already plan this generic theory elsewhere. The GlobalGaloisDeformations draft packet plans R04.1/R04.2 for an arbitrary profinite group with Φ_p (GL_n-valued: lifting functor, strict equivalence, universal framed and unframed rings, framed/unframed comparison), and the stage texts of R04.1/R04.2 are not GL_n-specific. PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22 route 1 (accepted) plans in layer (0) of GlobalGaloisDeformationsPartIIGValuedLifting 'the G-valued standing hypotheses and multiplier-fixed lifting functors' for global fields including function fields. The finding missed one further claimant: PAPER-PASKUNAS-QUAST-26 route 2 (accepted) sends the G-valued framed functor D^□_{ρ,G} 'for G smooth affine over O and Γ with Mazur's p-finiteness' (its /17), its pro-representability with tangent space Z^1 (/18) and its presentation by Z^1 generators and h^2 relations (/20) to LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1. So Ĝ-valued deformation functors are planned in three or four places. The route reason's case against GlobalGaloisDeformations ('over number fields', GL_n/polarized) does not apply to statements about an arbitrary Γ. FKP-22's reason distinguishes its Part II from this one by method (Khare-Wintenberger versus Ramakrishna), which is true for the global theorems but not for the shared functor layer. Right fix: one owner for G-valued deformation functors of a profinite group satisfying Φ_l. The framed functor, its representability and its presentation are already at R08.1 through the accepted PQ26 route, so import them from there. Route item 12's unframed part (Lemma 5.1, Definitions 5.2-5.4, Remark 5.3, Propositions 5.5-5.6) and Lemma 5.9 as a source of GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1/R04.2 in Ĝ-valued generality, next to the unframed GL_n theory. Alternatively, if the fixer prefers FKP-22's layer (0), say so in both Part II briefs. Either way, record the owner in route 1's reason and in FKP-22's brief. Keep in GValuedDeformationsAndPotentialAutomorphy what is specific to Γ_{K,S} over a function field (items 15-18 and Proposition 5.12). Item 13 (Lemma 5.7, Proposition 5.8) is also abstract in Γ, but it is a device consumed only by this Part II and may stay there with a note saying so.

(a) The brief's first sentence says 'potentially and for every reductive group' and then, in the same sentence, 'G split semisimple'. Theorem 1.1 is stated for G split semisimple over F_q in both texts (v2 p. 2; Acta p. 2), and the extraction's own summary says 'every split semisimple group'. The abstract calls the dual group 'split reductive over Z', but G itself is semisimple. So the brief contradicts itself and the paper. One small inaccuracy in the finding: section 6 opens with Ĝ split reductive, and section 7's local calculation with G split reductive over O_K. Semisimplicity is imposed from Theorem 6.5 on and throughout sections 5 and 8-11 (simply connected and simple in sections 10-11). This does not change the conclusion. (b) The tests. For PGL_n the Part II's theorem yields only some finite K'/K. The paper says 'One expects that this theorem should be true with K' = K, but we are not able to prove this' (v2 p. 2, Acta p. 2), so K' = K can come only from L. Lafforgue (GS.6), not from this Part II. GL_n and tori are not semisimple: Lemma 5.1's vanishing of H^0 of the adjoint representation, and so the whole deformation theory, fails for them. They fall outside the theorem. For semisimple Ĝ, rank r = 0 forces Ĝ trivial, so the 'r = 0' test is vacuous rather than impossible, but it is still no test. The finding's replacement is sound: 'split semisimple' in the first sentence, and tests the Part II can meet. Examples are Ĝ = SL_2 (G = PGL_2), with dihedral Coxeter parameters (h = 2); the rank-one count g = h^1 + (r-1)#Q = #Q checked against dim S_infinity; and a comparison, not a derivation, with L. Lafforgue for PGL_n, which requires importing GS.6 (see finding 6).

Read at Mathlib 082e2d3 and in the declaration index. RootDatum is an abbrev at Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Defs.lean:109 ('RootPairing ι ℤ X₁ X₂'). RootPairing.flip is at Defs.lean:127 (it swaps roots and coroots, giving the dual datum), RootPairing.IsReduced is at Reduced.lean:50 and RootPairing.Base is at Base.lean:70. So the reduced, based root datum and its dual in item 3 are library material. The rest of the §2.1 package is split reductive groups over a connected base, the central quotients G/Q with the smoothness criterion, the adjoint group and its base change, and standard parabolics P_I = M_I N_I. RG2.5 does not plan these ('this layer owns the group and functorial duality data only'); ReductiveGroupsPartII's summary assigns them to the existing Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap. The note's 'exactly this package' is therefore an overstatement. Low severity is right: nothing changes what gets built. Keep RG2.5 for the dual group over Z, and correct the note. Optionally cite Tau Ceti's dynamic TauCeti.Cocharacter.parabolicFunctor and leviFunctor as partial library support. Checked in the v2 TeX and in the Acta text (pp. 97–98); the wording is identical. Theorem 11.9(ii) asks only for a cuspidal π over Q̄_l with π^{G(Ô_K)} ≠ 0, and (iii)–(iv) ask only for an integral spherical f with normalized Whittaker coefficient 1. Nothing ties π to the Coxeter homomorphism φ. Theorem 10.11, which the proof says this 'is the same as', has the relation χ_V(φ_λ(Frob_v)) = eigenvalue of T_{V,v} on π^{G(Ô_K)}. The proof of Theorem 11.8 then uses an f 'matched everywhere locally with φ_λ'. The letter φ is also reused for the embedding π → C_cusp in (iii). None of E1–E16 records this; E15 is the separate ρ versus ρ_λ slip in Theorem 11.8. Item 31 states Theorem 11.9 without the matching. Kind misprint is right, since the intended statement is clear from 'the same as Theorem 10.11'. As printed, Theorem 11.9 is true but weaker than intended. What fails is its use in the proof of Theorem 11.8, so 'affects: the proof' is more accurate than 'a stated result'. Either is defensible. The fix is right. The eigenvalue may be taken on π^{G(Ô_K)}, as Theorem 10.11 does, or on π_v^{G(O_{K_v})}; the two are the same because the spherical line is one-dimensional. Severity medium is fair, because item 31 as written would be formalized without its essential conclusion.

Checked Appendix A §3 in v2 and on Acta p. 100 by page image; the text is the same in both. The definition literally reads 'Ē_Ť^{w′} is non-isomorphic to Ē_Ť for any w′ ∈ W'. This fails for w′ = 1, so it should read w′ ≠ 1. The claim 'Ē_Ť1 is automatically strongly regular … because the derived group of 𝒢_1 is simply connected' is false. The derived group of G ×^{Z(G)} T′ is isomorphic to that of G, so the intended statement is presumably about Ǧ_1 (G_1 has connected centre). The counterexample defeats either reading, and I checked it step by step. G_2 is simply connected and adjoint, so G_1 = G_2 × T′, W acts trivially on Ť′, and strong regularity of Ē_Ť1 is equivalent to that of Ē_Ť. The positive roots α, β, α+β, 2α+β, 3α+β, 3α+2β reduce modulo 2 to α, β, α+β, β, α+β, α; none is 0 in the root lattice (= X^*(Ť)). Hence every root is non-trivial on Ť[2], which makes Ē_Ť regular as [BG02, Prop. 2.2.9] requires, and Z(Ť[2])° = Ť. The Coxeter element is rotation by π/3. So det(1 − w) = |1 − e^{iπ/3}|² = 1, giving Ť^w = 1, and w³ = −1. Hence w acts on Ť[2] with order exactly 3. An elliptic curve with Frobenius of order 3 on X[2] exists, for example y² = x³ − x + 1 over F_3, whose 2-division cubic has no root in F_3. Both Frobenius on X[2] and w on Ť[2] are elements of order 3 in GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3, hence conjugate, so the identification exists and Fr^*Ē_Ť ≅ Ē_Ť^w. The Weil image ⟨Ť[2], w̃⟩ is finite, because w̃^6 is central and so trivial. In characteristic 0 it is therefore completely reducible, and any torus centralizing it lies in Ť ∩ Ť^w = 1. So the Weil Ǧ-local system is irreducible. But −1 ∈ W fixes Ť[2] pointwise, so strong regularity fails. The orthogonality (11.14) in v2, which is (A.5) in Acta and is quoted from [BG08, Prop. 10.6], is derived from strong regularity, so the general argument has a gap. I also verified that the application is safe. For a Coxeter parameter, φ^ad(Frob)^h lies in (T^ad)^w, whose order |det(1 − w)| = #Z_Ĝ is prime to t. So the geometric image already contains the order-t group, and its t-part lift is a non-zero v ∈ T̂[t]^{w=q} with Stab_W(v) = 1 (proof of Proposition 10.2(iv)). None of E1–E16 records this, and item 28 presents the reduction as valid. Kind error, affecting the proof of Appendix A's general claim, is right; the finding rightly leaves open whether the general cuspidality statement is true. The fix is right.

Checked the table (v2 p. 10: 'l ∤ n+1' in type A_n) and the proof of Theorem 5.13 (v2 p. 21; Acta pp. 30–31, same wording). SL_n is of type A_{n−1}, so l = 2 is very good for SL_n when n is odd, and 'n ≥ 2, hence l > 2 (because we work in very good characteristic)' is a non-sequitur. The only place the proof needs l > 2 is Gaitsgory's theorem, which the paper quotes as 'proved for l > 2'. One caveat. §5.1 contains the sentence 'We now suppose that we are given a representation i : Ĝ → GL(V) … l > 2(dim V − 1)', and §5.2 'keeps the assumptions of §5.1'. If that sentence were standing, l > 2 would follow, since dim V ≥ 2. But Theorem 5.14 restates that hypothesis, and the proof of 5.13 appeals to very good characteristic instead. So the natural reading is that it is local to Lemma 5.7 and Proposition 5.8, and on that reading Theorem 5.13 is unproved for n odd and l = 2, as the finding says. Harmless downstream: the only use is Theorem 5.14 for SL(V) with l > 2(dim V − 1) ≥ 2. Item 16 omits l > 2. It writes GL_n(k̄((t))), where the paper has GL_n of the algebraic closure of k((t)) (\overline{k((t))}); these are different fields. Not in E1–E16, since E10(a) is a different slip in the proof of 5.14. The fix is right.

The first half rests on the same misreading as finding 1. In this paper, 'the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^ad' is the stabilizer of ρ̄ under conjugation by Ĝ^ad. Scheme-theoretically it is trivial exactly when Z_Ĝ(ρ̄) = Z_Ĝ (lift fppf-locally through Ĝ → Ĝ^ad). That is precisely the introduction's 'the centralizer in Ĝ … is the centre of Ĝ'; the introduction only omits the word 'scheme-theoretically', which is normal informality there. The Q_8 group does satisfy the hypothesis: its stabilizer in PGL_2 is Z_{GL_2}(Q_8)/G_m = 1. The second half is technically true: a non-split extension of two distinct characters has scalar commutant. The proof is that any endomorphism preserves the unique stable line, and A − a·1 then maps the quotient χ_2 to a χ_2-line, of which there is none. But the paragraph is about pseudocharacters, which by the preceding sentence correspond to completely reducible representations, and Theorem 4.10 assumes absolute complete reducibility. For semisimple representations, the Schur equivalence the introduction states is correct. So the introduction does not misdescribe the hypothesis, and it is not the source of finding 1. The locator should also be Acta p. 4, not p. 3. The proposed correction would introduce an error: 'implies … absolute irreducibility' fails without complete reducibility (the Borel subgroup of GL_2 has trivial stabilizer in PGL_2).

Checked the statement and proof in v2 (pp. 23–24) and Acta (statement p. 34, sequence p. 35); the text is identical. Write M = ĝ_k. For v ∈ S, local duality and the hypothesis give H^2(K_v, M) = 0. So the kernel of H^2(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, M) → ⊕_{v∈Q} H^2(K_v, M) equals the kernel of the map to ⊕_{v∈S∪Q}, and by Poitou–Tate that kernel is dual to Ш^1_{S∪Q}(M^∨(1)). A class of H^1(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, M^∨(1)) that is trivial at Q is unramified there, so Ш^1_{S∪Q} is the subgroup of H^1_{Q-triv}(Γ_{K,S}) of classes also trivial at S; it is not all of H^1_{Q-triv}. With Euler characteristic 0 and h^0 = 0: h^1(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, M) = dim Ш^1_{S∪Q} + r#Q. For Q = ∅ this gives h^1(Γ_{K,S}, M) = dim Ш^1_S(M^∨(1)). Greenberg–Wiles gives h^1(Γ_{K,S}, M^∨(1)) = dim Ш^1_S(M) + Σ_{v∈S} h^0(K_v, M). So equality holds iff the localization of H^1(Γ_{K,S}, M^∨(1)) to S vanishes. Nothing forces this, because h^1(K_v, M^∨(1)) = h^0(K_v, M), which is at least r when ρ̄ is unramified at v ∈ S. The hypothesis H^0(K_v, M^∨(1)) = 0 can still hold in that case, for example when q_v ≢ 1 mod l and no Frobenius eigenvalue is q_v^{-1}. The consequence h^1(Γ_{K,S∪Q}, M) = r#Q survives, as the finding says. The only use is with S = ∅: §8.4, 'Let q = h^1(Γ_{K,∅}, ĝ_k)'. E8 and E9 concern other slips in the same proposition, and E8's reason uses the Q = ∅ equality. All three fixes work. For the second: H^0(K_v, M) = 0 and H^0(K_v, M^∨(1)) = 0 give H^1(K_v, M^∨(1)) = 0 by the local Euler characteristic. The third requires dropping the second equality in (i).

Confirmed except element (g), which should be dropped. Each element was checked in the v2 TeX and located in the Acta text. (a) Acta p. 30: 'identity component of H is semisimple … because Ĝ is semisimple' is false. N(T) ⊂ SL_2 is irreducible with identity component a torus, and a dihedral lift with infinite-order character realizes it. The needed conclusion holds as the finding says. det W restricted to H° is an H-invariant character. A non-zero H-invariant cocharacter of Z(H°)° would give a torus centralized by H, hence a proper Levi containing H, which Ĝ-irreducibility forbids. So det W is trivial on H° and factors through H/H°. This is a false statement, so kind 'error' (affects the proof) fits better than 'gap'. Item 14 does not actually repeat the false step: it compresses it to 'reductive, and constituents have finite-order determinant'. (b) Acta p. 14: the paper's G is reductive there, and 'g is semisimple' fails for tori and GL_n. Item 5 copies it. (c) Acta p. 78: the image of each composite is the decomposition group D_w. As w runs over the places above v′, these run over all H-conjugates of D, so equality at every w forces H = C_H(D)·D, in particular D normal. This fails for S_3 with D of order 2. The only use (proof of Proposition 9.5) needs no local condition, so it affects nothing. Item 23 copies 'at each place'. (d) Acta p. 81: in type D_4 the exponents 1, 3, 3, 5 give the eigenvalue q^3 = −1 twice. Only the simplicity of q (exponent 1) is used. This is a false statement affecting nothing. (e) Acta p. 45: U = G(O_K) there, which has no normal pro-p subgroup with quotient T(F_q). U_0/U_p with U_p the pro-p radical of the Iwahori is meant. (f) Acta pp. 18–19: 'étale at x' should be at (1, x), and 'η⫽G … étale at i(1, x)' should be at π_{X′}(i(1, x)); E12(e) records only G_k·φ(x). (h) The last application of Lemma 3.12 has A = O[X]^G, but L is algebraic over Frac O[X] and has positive transcendence degree over Frac O[X]^G. The repair works: replace L by its relative algebraic closure L_0 over Frac O[X]^G, which is Galois with group the image of 𝒢 because that field is algebraically closed in Frac O[X] for connected G. (i) Acta p. 61, with Definition 3.5(ii) on Acta p. 8: ρ̄_i ⊗ λ takes values in Ĝ(l), l ⊋ k, while the definition quantifies over ρ′ : Γ → G(k). The definition should quantify over k̄, which is what Corollary 10.8 verifies. (g) is not a mistake: G(O_{K_v}) sits in G(A_K) at v, so π^{G(O_{K_v})} = π_v^{G(O_{K_v})} ⊗ (the rest) is non-zero exactly when π_v^{G(O_{K_v})} is. None of (a)–(i) is in E1–E16.

Each part was checked against v2 and the Acta text. Item 4: Proposition 3.7(i) reads 'If Gamma is G-completely reducible, and L in P is a Levi subgroup containing Gamma, then Gamma in L is L-irreducible' (v2 p. 9, Acta p. 13). The item drops both hypotheses. Without them Gamma need not lie in any Levi of P, so the item's statement does not make sense. Item 6: Proposition 3.10(v) is about a point x in X(k) with closed G_k-orbit and a G-invariant open U containing x, and it produces f with f(x) != 0 (v2 p. 11, Acta p. 15). As the item states it, f = 0 satisfies everything (D_X(0) is empty), so the statement is vacuous. Item 13's note is false. Besides l > 2(dim V - 1), the paper imposes l > 2 dim g (Proposition 6.7), l > 2 dim G (Proposition 9.5), l > 2h - 2 (Definition 10.9 and Proposition 10.10), l not dividing #W (section 7 and section 8.4) and q = 1 mod l (section 7). The brief itself lists some of these. Item 15's note is wrong. h^1 = h^2 gives only a balanced presentation O[[X_1..X_g]]/(f_1..f_g). It becomes a complete intersection once R/pi is finite (Theorem 5.13, via de Jong/Gaitsgory), and then R is finite flat over O of Krull dimension 1; dimension zero holds only for R/pi or R[1/l]. Item 26: Definition 10.9 and Proposition 10.10 both lie on v2 p. 57, and Theorem 10.11 starts p. 58, as I checked by extracting the pages one at a time. Item 35: in the paper the dense subspace is sum_P Eis_P C_0(...)^U of compactly supported pseudo-Eisenstein series, Eis_P phi(g) = sum over P(K)\G(K) of phi(gamma g) (v2 p. 43). In this paper 'geometric Eisenstein series' means Braverman-Gaitsgory's (section 10), so the item's wording misleads. The item also uses R, m_R and the rho_i without the hypotheses of Proposition 8.12. Item 36: Corollary 8.21 asserts only a cuspidal Pi with Pi^U != 0 and the Hecke-eigenvalue identity (v2 p. 46). Definition 8.7's warning says this is a priori weaker than 'automorphic'. The Whittaker clause needs a minimal prime p of B(U,O)_m and a fixed psi, and global genericity needs psi generic. q in 'g = qr' is h^1(Gamma_{K,empty}, g_k) (v2 p. 48, Acta p. 73), not #F_q. Refinements to the fix. (i) Item 27 does not differ from the paper. It copies it: both v2 p. 57 and Acta p. 86 print 'Let G denote a split reductive group over K', although section 10.2 and section 8 work with G over F_q. The slip is harmless, because a split reductive group over K is the base change of a Chevalley group over F_q, which gives G(O^_K). So 'as G(O^_K) requires' overstates it. If the item is changed to F_q, PROTOCOL section 18 requires a new sourceIssue (misprint, affects nothing, present in both texts), not a silent correction. (ii) For item 36, say that automorphy in the sense of Definition 8.7 is how the paper uses the corollary in section 11, via Lemma 8.8 under Zariski density. It does follow directly from f_m being an isomorphism, by Lemma 8.19 and Theorem 4.5, but the paper does not state it, so mark it editorial. (iii) In item 35, restore the other data of Proposition 8.12 too: residue characteristic l != p, U_v = G(O_{K_v}) outside S, and the Hecke characters phi_{i,v} valued in R.
